Messages.Author: Vincent Price
Messages.Body:
If a vampire sends a another vampire to torpor via the Wooden Stake
and I decapitate the vampire going to torpor, do I lose the wooden
stake?

Wood stake says "Strength damage each strike. If more than 1 damage
is inflicted on an opposing vampire by this weapon in a given combat,
then that vampire is sent into torpor. In that case, this card is
transferred to that vampire, and he or she doesn't untap as normal
during the untap phase as long as he or she remains in torpor."
Decapitate "Only usable when the opposing vampire is going into
torpor; not usable by a vampire going into torpor. Burn the opposing
vampire instead of sending that vampire to torpor."

Vincent Price
V:KEN Prince of Seattle

>
> If a vampire sends a another vampire to torpor via the Wooden Stake

Yes. All cards on a burned vampire are burned.

> > > stake?

>
> does the burned minion get the stake in the first place? Stake says minion
> going to torpor gets stake, when decapitate says no torpor, burned.

All of the stake's effects resolve before decapitate so the stake sends the
minion on it's way to torpor and hence the minion gets the stake. Then,
because the minion is going to torpor you can play decapitate ( if you meet
the other requirements ) which then burns the minion rather then actually
allowing it to go to torpor.

I would also imagine that if you get staked and play Undead Persistence that
you will not got to torpor and now possess a stake which you could
potentially give back :)

But it is 02:35 here and I'm getting notorious for forgetting small details
at this time in the morning so I'm quite possibly wrong :}
